entry.name: Humanoid Everyday
entry.title: Humanoid Everyday: A Comprehensive Robotic Dataset for Open-World Humanoid Manipulation
entry.summary: Teleoperated Unitree G1 and H1 humanoids on 246 everyday tasks; the G1 episodes carry Unitree Dex3-1 hand pressure sensors (9 per hand).
entry.hand: Unitree Dex3-1 (7 DoF) x 2 on G1; Inspire (6 DoF) x 2 on H1

sensor.note: G1 episodes only: observation.tactile.values (18, 4) float32 + sensor_id 1-18, NaN-padded to 4. The release's observation.tactile.values (18, 4) is shifted by 13 values: the recording code (GitHub teleop/master.py + worker.py, commit 9611546) writes 13 odometry values and then 216 pressure values (left 9 x 12, then right 9 x 12) but reads the pressure block from where the odometry starts, reshapes to 18 x 12 and keeps indices [0, 2, 9, 11] or [3, 6, 8] per row. Release row k, kept index i is true value p = 12(k-1) + i - 13 (hand p // 108, sensor (p % 108) // 12, element p % 12; p < 0 = odometry), so a release row is not a sensor. After undoing the shift only 22 of the 66 Dex3-1 readings survive (12 left, 10 right); the right hand's palm 2 and 3 fall off the end, the other kept values are 30000 (no reading) or odometry (release row 1 and row 2 col 0). H1/Inspire episodes have empty tactile arrays.

scale.text: Paper: 10.3k trajectories, 260 tasks in 7 categories, 3M+ frames @30 Hz. HF release: 8,949 episodes, 246 tasks, 3,436,171 frames (~31.8 h); tactile G1 part: 4,064 episodes, 124 tasks, ~16.5 h

entry.access: Hugging Face USC-PSI-Lab/humanoid-everyday, ungated, LeRobot v2.1, one parquet per episode (~935 GB, depth and LiDAR inside the parquet); tactile only in the G1 episodes of this full release, not in the lite G1/H1 repos.
caveats: Tactile only on G1 / Dex3-1 episodes (4,064); H1 / Inspire episodes have empty tactile arrays.

observation.tactile.values is shifted by 13 values relative to the Dex3-1 pressure array (recording-code bug): release row 1 and the first value of row 2 hold odometry, every other kept value belongs to a different sensor than its sensor_id, and only 22 of 66 readings survive (12 left, 10 right; right palm 2-3 lost). The viewer undoes the shift.

Units are not documented, and Unitree's sensor-to-finger map could not be read (the order used comes from third-party G1 code); values sit near 101 kPa and rise by at most a few hundred units during manipulation.
The lite repos Humanoid-Everyday-G1/-H1 carry only joints, actions and video: no tactile, depth, LiDAR, IMU or odometry.
meta/episodes.jsonl 'instruction' is the same string for all 8,949 episodes; use meta/tasks.jsonl via task_index.
License differs between sources: HF card says Apache-2.0, GitHub README says MIT.
Release (8,949 episodes, 246 tasks) is smaller than the paper's 10.3k / 260; 5 episodes were dropped for zero valid frames.

unconfirmed: hours=31.8 derived from the HF release: 3,436,171 frames / 30 fps. G1 part: 1,779,287 frames (16.5 h), H1 part: 1,656,884 frames (15.3 h), from meta/episodes.jsonl lengths.
Tactile task count 124 = distinct task_index over robot_type 'g1' episodes in meta/episodes.jsonl; tasks are split 124 G1 / 122 H1 with no task on both robots.

taxels_per_hand=33, coverage and range are Unitree's Dex3-1 product spec (9 sensors: 2x2 palm x3, 2x2 finger pad x3, 3x1 fingertip x3); the paper only says the Dex3-1 hands 'possess tactile sensors'. Release-to-sensor mapping: the 13-value shift is derived from the release's recording code (teleop/master.py + worker.py at 9611546) and checked on all frames of the 8 sampled episodes: release row 1 and row 2 col 0 equal odometry position x, z and quat w, y, z (max |diff| 0), and every recovered non-30000 value lands on its true sensor's element set (A = 0, 2, 9, 11 on pads and palm, B = 3, 6, 8 on fingertips; 0 violations). Surviving readings per hand (sensor, element): thumb pad 11, thumb tip 8, middle pad 2 and 11, middle tip 8, index pad 2 and 11, index tip 8, palm 1 2 and 11, plus left palm 2 and palm 3 element 11. Sensor order per hand (thumb pad, thumb tip, middle pad, middle tip, index pad, index tip, palm 1-3) is from third-party G1 code (i2ca/prometheus-vla g1_utils.py), not a Unitree document; the data agree (only sensors 2, 4, 6 carry type-B readings). Left-first order is from the recording code and agrees with joints and video in one-handed episodes 3422, 8208, 8174.

Unit not stated; readings near 1.01e5 suggest absolute pressure in Pa (inferred from magnitude). Rises above the episode's 5th percentile were 32-720 units in 10 sampled G1 episodes, and <=50 in episode 0 while the left hand holds a phone stand, so contact visibility is unverified.

22 live release cells (column 0 of rows 3-18, column 2 of rows 3, 5, 7, 12, 14, 16) and the odometry in rows 1-2 were observed in 20 of 20 random G1 episodes, not all 4,064; after the shift these are the 22 readings listed above.
Camera model D435 is from the GitHub README calibration section; the paper says only 'Intel RealSense RGB-D'. Head mount not stated; inferred from the egocentric view.
LiDAR unit not stated; point norms of ~4,000 suggest millimetres. Depth stored as float32 converted from uint16 (he2lerobot.py); depth unit not stated.
Accelerometer magnitude ~9.87 in episode 0 suggests m/s^2; IMU/odometry units not stated. Odometry is all zeros in the H1 episode checked (40).
Number of scenes, objects and operators not stated; paper says 'indoor and outdoor environments'.
Raw per-task zips (with AVP head/wrist poses, tau_ff, sensor_type) are linked from a Google spreadsheet in the README; that sheet was not opened.

channels.note: Kept indices per row [0, 2, 9, 11] or [3, 6, 8] (NaN-padded to 4), chosen by the recording code per release row, not per true sensor. Live: column 0 of rows 3-18 and column 2 of rows 3, 5, 7, 12, 14, 16 (22 cells) = 12 left and 10 right true readings (right palm 2-3 lost). Constant 30000 elsewhere. Row 1 (all 4) and row 2 column 0 equal odometry position x, z and quat w, y, z. Row 15 column 0 (= right index pad element 2) has a ~2 kPa higher baseline.

episode_index.where: meta/episodes.jsonl (episode_index, tasks, length, robot_type, instruction) + meta/tasks.jsonl (task, category, description)
episode_index.note: 8,949 episodes: 4,064 G1 (tactile) + 4,885 H1. 2-80 episodes per task (median 40). G1 durations 3.9-80.1 s (median 13.6 s; 81% within 10-60 s). Categories (all/G1 tasks): Basic 64/15, Articulated 48/22, Locomanip 47/47, HRI 41/16, deformable 19/10, Tool_use 19/11, Precision 8/3. No scene, object or operator labels. 5 episodes dropped (meta/errors.jsonl); their parquets are still in the repo.

sample.reason: Public, ungated HF release under Apache-2.0 (dataset card; the GitHub README says MIT); both allow redistribution with attribution. Tactile exists only in the G1 / Dex3-1 episodes, so only G1 episodes are sampled. Each episode is one single-row-group parquet, so the tactile, joint, IMU, odometry and action columns can be range-read without the depth column.

episodes.why: G1, task_index 85. Pour, one hand. Contact 4.0-6.2 s (kettle grasp; the hand is just right of the frame) and 14.5-14.9 s (release), 2.9 s total; peak +17.9 kPa on id 15 col 0; ids 16 col 0/2 and 12 col 2 also rise. Task 84 (pour_water_from_a_kettle_into_a_cup) holds the same 40 recordings as task 85: same file sizes for all 40 pairs, identical tactile/joint/action columns in ep 3382 vs 3422.
G1, task_index 227. Wipe, one hand with a tool. One continuous contact 9.8-13.0 s (3.2 s) while the duster is pressed on the table; peak +22.8 kPa on id 16 col 2.

G1, task_index 221. Twist, two hands (left holds the bottle, right turns the cap). Contact 21.2-22.6 s (1.4 s, cap twist); peak +15.3 kPa on id 16 col 2. Only 2 of 40 episodes in this task have a contiguous >= 1 s contact.
G1, task_index 226. Pull out a plug, one hand. Contact 4.5-8.8 s (3.9 s continuous from 4.9 s) while gripping and pulling the plug; peak +32.4 kPa on id 16 col 2, the largest rise among the picks.
G1, task_index 151. Two-handed lift and handover to a person. Contact 5.9-9.3 s (3.3 s) while both hands hold the ball; peak +1.8 kPa on id 15 col 0, smaller rise on id 16 col 0.

G1, task_index 120. Deformable object, two hands spreading the opening. Contact 5.9-9.2 s (2.7 s continuous); peak +2.3 kPa on id 15 col 0, id 16 col 0/2 also rise. The best of 31 episodes >= 10 s in this task; 8 of the other 9 G1 deformable tasks show no >= 1 s contact in any episode checked.

G1, task_index 214. Outdoor scene (task text: 'A chair is kept outside'; brick paving in the video), walk then pull. Contact 6.1-9.0 s (1.9 s longest run); peak +13.5 kPa on id 15 col 0. Only 1 of the task's 3 episodes shows contact.
G1, task_index 20. Articulated object on the floor, two hands, pull upwards to extend. Contact 11.5-13.9 s (2.4 s); peak +9.3 kPa on id 16 col 2, also id 9 col 0 (+0.6 kPa).

sample.fetch_estimate: ~120 MB for the conversion: per episode the non-depth, non-LiDAR columns (0.20-0.43 MB, by parquet column-chunk sizes) plus the LiDAR column (9.7-20.5 MB) and the mp4 (0.55-1.13 MB); ~10 MB without LiDAR. The full 8 parquets would be 1.12 GB (depth 88-197 MB each). Already downloaded in this step: the 8 mp4s (6.6 MB) and tactile/sensor_id/timestamp/index column chunks of 1,421 G1 episodes (~35-55 KB each).
sample.rules_applied: 8 of 246 release tasks, all from the 124 G1 tasks (H1 episodes have empty tactile arrays). Chosen to cover 7 categories (Basic, Tool_use, Precision x2, HRI, deformable, Locomanip, Articulated), actions pour / wipe / twist / pull-out / handover / spread / walk+pull / extend, desk, floor and outdoor scenes, and one- and two-handed tasks. One episode per task, 8 in total. Durations 12.5-27.5 s, so no window is needed. Tactile check: observation.tactile.values and observation.tactile.sensor_id were range-read for 1,421 G1 episodes of 10-60 s (up to 8 per task for all 124 tasks, then all in-range episodes of 24 candidate tasks). Every picked episode has (18,4) values and sensor ids 1-18 in every frame and no NaN in the 22 live cells. The release-wide faults are present in all of them and cannot be avoided: id 1 cols 0-3 equal odometry position x, z and quat w, y, and id 2 col 0 equals odometry quat z (verified per frame); 39 cells are a constant 30000 and 6 are NaN. One episode checked (7073, door handle) has a frame with only 17 sensors and was not picked. Contact = any live cell above its first-second median + 100 Pa (noise MAD 0-12 Pa, values come in 8 Pa steps), for a contiguous run of at least 1 s; picked episodes have runs of 1.4-3.9 s. Contact is sparse in this release: of the 1,229 episodes in the broad pass, 122 have >= 1 s in total above that threshold and 55 a contiguous >= 1 s run; 67 of 119 tasks had no episode with >= 1 s of contact, among them both eraser-wiping tasks, fold_towel, insert_flower_into_vase and open_a_drawer_g1. In each picked episode only 1-4 live cells rise above 100 Pa (mostly id 15 col 0 and id 16 col 2); the others stay within the noise. Each mp4 was decoded: H.264 yuv420p 640x480 with as many frames as parquet rows, and frames at contact onset and peak show the described task. subject is null: operators are not labelled. scene is taken from the task description and the video, since the release has no scene labels.

visualization.detail: Un-shifted to the true Dex3-1 sensors (the release's array starts 13 values early, inside the odometry; index arithmetic from the release's recording code, teleop/master.py + worker.py at 9611546). 22 recorded readings (12 left, 10 right) as cells on a schematic hand per side: fingertip 3x1 and pad 2x2 blocks for thumb, index, middle, three 2x2 palm pads; the 44 readings the release does not contain are hollow 'inactive' squares. Values = raw minus first-second median, fixed per-episode range. Plots: per-region sums and per-sensor sums per hand.
